articles.title: CM: Won’t shield Chorbagan guilty, will release probe panel findings
articles.summary: CM Suvendu Adhikari vows no one will be shielded in Chorbagan stampede probe; panel report and safety steps to be public; meeting with puja organisers planned.
articles.body: Kolkata: None responsible for the Chorbagan stampede that claimed 19 lives will be shielded, CM Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday, adding that the state will make the probe panel’s findings along with its safety recommendations public. He also hinted at convening a meeting of Durga Puja organisers as early as Jan-end to chalk out steps to prevent similar incidents during next year’s festival.Asserting that this year’s Durga Puja has taught the state an important lesson in religious responsibility and peaceful coexistence, Adhikari said people have realised that responsibility to protect one’s religion rests with each individual.“Dharma jar jar, utsab sabar (religion is specific to individuals, festival is for all). But religion is personal, and the responsibility to protect one’s religion is one’s own. Everyone in West Bengal has understood this during this year’s Durga Puja. This is the new West Bengal, the West Bengal of change,” the CM said at a Bijoya Sammilani event attended by representatives of 6,000 puja committees at Milan Mela Prangan. The usual fanfare associated with such a programme was scaled down in view of the Chorbagan tragedy.Expressing profound grief over the deaths and describing the incident as “deeply distressing”, Adhikari said, “The inquiry into the Chorbagan tragedy has been entrusted with a retired judge following Calcutta High Court Chief Justice’s advice. The govt will not shield anyone. The recommendations on safety and security will be compiled in the form of a booklet and given to puja organisers.”Taking a dig at the previous Mamata Banerjee-led govt, he said, “I will not refer to the tragedy as either a small incident or a conspiracy.”Citing large gatherings expected during Chhath and the popularity of Kali Puja in Naihati and Barasat, Jagaddhatri Puja in Krishnanagar and Chandernagore and Kartik Puja in Hooghly’s Bansberia, the CM said the administration will work to keep the remaining festivals incident-free. He sought cooperation of the organisers and other stakeholders to ensure that lessons from Chorbagan translate into adoption of concrete safety measures.Adhikari is likely to hold a meeting with Kali Puja organisers on Wednesday on security parameters.The CM claimed apart from the Chorbagan tragedy, this year’s Durga Puja celebrations were conducted in a disciplined manner and immersions held without any restrictions. He cited examples of certain locations in Murshidabad, East Midnapore, South 24 Parganas, Malda, Diamond Harbour and North Dinajpur to claim that immersion processions proceeded peacefully in these areas unlike previous years.“I do not blame any community. I blame those who were in the administration earlier and surrendered,” he said, asserting that people from different communities cooperated during the festival.Adhikari also addressed the controversy over the transfer of 25 people injured in the Chorbagan stampede from govt hospitals to private facilities. “There was no failure here. articles.title: SC restores Karnataka land, says government can acquire only for public purpose
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Holding that govt can acquire land from citizens only for public purpose and not for the benefit of some person or organisation, Supreme Court
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Holding that govt can acquire land from citizens only for public purpose and not for the benefit of some person or organisation, Supreme Court Monday quashed a 1988 acquisition of about 59 acres of land near Bengaluru by Karnataka govt for a cooperative housing society and restored the land to its owners after 38 years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating “the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens”. It said that illegal acquisitions were made through fraud and undue influence and directed the state govt to pay Rs 50,000 to all litigant landowners who had challenged the process.“Condemnation of privately owned land for public purpose can only be with authority of law and with just compensation being paid. That such authority of law can be exercised only for public purpose is without cavil, with just compensation being an ancillary right, which does not by itself justify an acquisition. However just the compensation be, if the authority of law is lacking or the public purpose is absent, there can be no eminent domain exercised,” the court said.SC upheld the single-bench HC order,which said that it was at the instigation of middlemen that the state employed its machinery to acquire land for the society.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Minimum temperatures drop across state; Jalgaon coolest at 15.4°C, NDA in Pune 15.6°C
articles.summary: Maharashtra sees sharp dip in minimum temperatures as dry northwesterly winds prevail; Jalgaon coolest at 15.4°C, Pune NDA 15.6°C; cyclone may raise lows after Oct 28.
articles.body: Pune: A sharp drop in night temperatures swept across Maharashtra on Monday, with Jalgaon emerging as the state’s coolest location at 15.4°C, followed by NDA in Pune at 15.6°C.Dry northwesterly winds and clear skies brought a sharp decline in night temperatures across the city, with the minimum at Shivajinagar dropping to 17.4°C, down from 20.4°C a day earlier. The maximum temperature stood at 34.2°C — a wide day-night temperature difference of 16.8°C. NDA’s 15.6°C was the lowest of the season so far at the station.Relative humidity at 5.30pm was 29% at Shivajinagar and just 18% at Lohegaon. The latter recorded a maximum of 34.6°C and a minimum of 17.7°C.“Northwesterly winds are dominating most parts of Maharashtra. Minimum temperatures are dropping, while daytime temperatures are still reaching around 35°C. Dry air intrusion and clear skies are allowing greater radiational cooling at night, resulting in the fall in minimum temperatures,” India Meteorological Department (IMD) scientist SD Sanap said.Among the other relatively cool locations in Maharashtra on Monday were Washim and Yavatmal, both at 16°C, followed by Nashik (16.2°C), Gondia (16.5°C), Parbhani (16.9°C) and Mahabaleshwar (17°C).Residents in the city reported discomfort amid the dry conditions. “It has been extremely dry lately. The sudden drop in temperatures and the big difference between day and night temperatures means that we have to not only face hotter afternoons but also cooler nights. I am also experiencing sinus issues,” Kalyaninagar resident Pragya Saha said.Low humidity can dry and irritate the nasal passages, sinuses and throat, worsening discomfort among people prone to sinus problems. The dry conditions may ease somewhat towards the end of the week, with the approaching cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal expected to bring some moisture into parts of Maharashtra.Cyclonic storm Arnab over the westcentral Bay of Bengal was centred about 490km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha and 490km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 5.30pm on Monday. IMD said it was likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by the forenoon of Oct 28, with sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph and gusts of up to 140 kmph.“After Oct 28-29, minimum temperatures are likely to rise because of moisture incursion under the influence of the cyclone,” Sanap said.Isolated rainfall could not be ruled out in parts of Madhya Maharashtra and Marathwada, as well as eastern Vidarbha. However, widespread or heavy rainfall was not expected in these regions, he said.Pune city is not expected to receive significant rainfall. IMD’s local forecast, however, indicates the possibility of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning, light to moderate rain and gusty winds at isolated places in the Pune Ghats on Thursday (Oct 29).For Tuesday, IMD has forecast a maximum temperature of 34°C and a minimum of 18°C in the city, with mainly clear skies becoming partly cloudy towards the evening.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: In 2024, Jessica Alba helped promote a baby photo contest that became a major charity fundraiser; by 2026, the campaign had generated more than $45 million in grants for Baby2Baby to help children in need across the US
articles.summary: A baby photo contest backed by actress Jessica Alba has grown into a major fundraising initiative, generating more than $45 million in grants for
articles.body: A baby photo contest backed by actress Jessica Alba has grown into a major fundraising initiative, generating more than $45 million in grants for nonprofit organisation Baby2Baby since 2024. The campaign supports children and families across the United States by helping provide essential items such as diapers, formula, food and clothing.The initiative, called Baby of the Year, is returning for its third edition in 2026. Championed by Baby2Baby ambassadors Jessica Alba, Paris Hilton and Jenna Dewan, the nationwide competition invites parents and legal guardians to submit photos and profiles of their little ones, with the winner receiving $25,000 and an opportunity to appear in a national advertising campaign.According to an announcement by fundraiser Colossal, the grants generated through the competition have helped Baby2Baby distribute essential supplies to children in all 50 states, support disaster relief efforts and invest in infrastructure to strengthen its long-term work.How Jessica Alba's baby photo contest raises money for charityThe Baby of the Year competition combines a nationwide search for an adorable young champion with fundraising for children in need. Parents submit a photograph and a short profile explaining what makes their child special. Friends, family members and supporters can then rally behind their favourite entries through multiple rounds of voting.Supporters can vote for free, while additional votes can be cast through donations under the competition's official rules. The donations are managed by DTCare, a registered US public charity, which will issue a grant to Baby2Baby after the competition concludes.Baby2Baby provides diapers, formula, clothing, food and other basic necessities to children facing difficult circumstances. Its work also includes supporting families affected by disasters and strengthening programmes that help children across the country."We are enormously grateful for the support of the Baby of the Year competition for the third year in a row," Baby2Baby Co-CEOs Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein said in a statement."We are proud to partner on this transformative campaign that raises critical funds for Baby2Baby's mission, ensuring that we can provide more than one million children across the country with the basic essentials they deserve for years to come," they added.Jessica Alba, Paris Hilton and Jenna Dewan champion the initiativeJessica Alba, who founded The Honest Company in 2012, is a longtime Baby2Baby board member and an advocate for women and children's welfare. Her involvement brings together her work in the business world and her commitment to causes supporting families.Paris Hilton, a Baby2Baby Angel, has also used her public platform to highlight children's rights and wellbeing. Through her nonprofit, 11:11 Media Impact, she has supported advocacy efforts related to child welfare and institutional child abuse reform.Actor Jenna Dewan, known for films and television projects including Step Up, The Rookie and Supergirl, is another longtime Baby2Baby Angel supporting the campaign.The 2026 competition is also backed by brands including The Honest Company, Graco and Shutterfly, which support the initiative's focus on families, childhood and the preservation of memories.What does the Baby of the Year winner receive?The winner will receive $25,000 and appear in nationwide, multichannel advertising campaigns. The prize package includes exposure through The Honest Company's social media channels and official website, advertising featuring Honest products, and an advertorial in Variety magazine.The competition has already crowned two winners. Luca won the 2025 title, while Sloane Maya was named Baby of the Year in 2024. Sloane was affectionately described by her family as a "miracle baby".Colossal says the competition operates under a trust and safety framework intended to protect participants and their families. Parents or legal guardians manage submissions, and photographs are used for identity verification and competition profile pages, subject to the official rules governing finalists and the grand prize winner.Registration for the 2026 competition is open through the official Baby of the Year website.Baby2Baby's work across the USBaby2Baby provides essential supplies to more than one million children across all 50 states. Over the past 15 years, the organisation says it has distributed more than half a billion items to children in homeless shelters, foster care, hospitals, domestic violence programmes and school districts, as well as to families affected by disasters.The $45 million in grants generated through the Baby of the Year campaign since 2024 adds to the support available for this work. The initiative demonstrates how a competition built around family photographs and community participation can also help raise funds for a larger charitable cause.Colossal, which runs purpose-driven online competitions to raise money for charitable organisations, says it has raised more than $243 million for charity since 2022.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2008, Peyton Manning began a gala for an Indianapolis children's hospital; 18 years later, its final edition raised over $4.2 million, taking the event's total to nearly $24 million
articles.summary: Peyton Manning’s long-running charitable effort for children’s healthcare in Indiana has reached a milestone, with the final Celebration of Caring Gala
articles.body: Peyton Manning’s long-running charitable effort for children’s healthcare in Indiana has reached a milestone, with the final Celebration of Caring Gala raising more than $4.2 million for Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital. The 18th edition of the fundraiser took place at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on February 13, 2026, marking the end of an event that has supported paediatric care in the state for nearly two decades. According to the Ascension St. Vincent Foundation’s announcement and Thespun, the latest fundraising total brings the gala’s cumulative contributions since 2008 to nearly $24 million. The annual event, organised by the foundation and led by the former Indianapolis Colts quarterback, has helped fund hospital programmes, medical technology and expansions designed to improve care for children. Although the gala is being retired, Manning has indicated that his involvement with the hospital and its mission will continue.A final edition with a lasting impactThe gala’s closing year was particularly significant because the funds will support a new outpatient paediatric dialysis unit at the hospital. The facility is intended to address a gap in specialised care for children with end-stage renal disease, who require ongoing treatment and medical supervision. A major contribution came from Aneel Bhusri, Manning’s friend, who pledged a $1.8 million matching donation during the event to mark its 18th year. The gift helped boost the evening’s fundraising total beyond $4.2 million.The hospital’s fundraising history reflects how the gala has evolved from a local charitable initiative into a major source of support for paediatric healthcare in Indianapolis. Reporting by local broadcaster WTHR, published through Yahoo Sports, also confirmed that Manning returned to the city for the final event and that his role as a supporter of the hospital would continue beyond the gala.Where the money has made a differenceOver the years, donations raised through the event have contributed to several improvements in children's healthcare. These include support for the hospital's paediatric intensive care unit, technology for Indiana's largest neonatal intensive care unit and broader investments in services for young patients and their families.The fundraising effort has also supported the hospital system's wider development goals, including its Care for Tomorrow campaign. Such investments are intended to strengthen the resources available to medical teams caring for children, from newborns requiring intensive treatment to patients managing complex, long-term conditions.The hospital's foundation has described Manning's involvement as central to the gala's success, crediting his sustained commitment with helping build support for the institution and its patients. The event's official fundraising page confirms that the initiative generated nearly $24 million over 18 years.The end of the gala, not the missionFor Manning, the final edition brings a long-running chapter of his charitable work in Indianapolis to a close. The decision to retire the event does not signal an end to his relationship with the hospital. articles.title: An Arizona home's construction blocked a neighbour's mountain view; court rules homeowners have no automatic right to unobstructed scenery
articles.summary: An Arizona Court of Appeals has ruled that homeowners have no automatic legal right to an unobstructed mountain view across a neighbour’s property,
articles.body: An Arizona Court of Appeals has ruled that homeowners have no automatic legal right to an unobstructed mountain view across a neighbour’s property, upholding the dismissal of a private nuisance claim. The case involved Tina and John Pavlak, whose neighbouring property in Mesa was approved for a house following a change to its building envelope. The couple argued that the proposed construction would obstruct their scenic view, reduce privacy and affect their property’s value. In its ruling, filed on 28 August 2026, the court found that Arizona law does not recognise loss of a view as grounds for a private nuisance claim.Why Arizona homeowners have no automatic right to a mountain viewAccording to the Arizona Court of Appeals’ judgment, Funk Family Enterprises LLC purchased Lot 10 in 2023. In 2024, the HOA and the City of Mesa approved requests to modify the building envelope, moving it uphill to improve the view from the proposed house on that property. Funk applied for a construction permit in March 2025. The Pavlaks subsequently brought legal action, seeking to prevent construction and challenging the proposed development on several grounds.The homeowners initially pursued claims including fraudulent schemes and artifices, unjust enrichment and fraudulent misrepresentation. After those claims were dismissed, they filed an amended complaint alleging violations of the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act and private nuisance. They argued that the proposed house would reduce their privacy, obstruct their view, diminish their property’s value and potentially cause rainwater runoff problems. They also alleged a $300,000 reduction in the value of Lot 11 and the loss of $287,107 in recent backyard improvements. The lower court denied their request for a preliminary injunction and dismissed their amended complaint. On appeal, the Pavlaks challenged the dismissal of their private nuisance claim.What Arizona's ruling means for blocked mountain viewsIn considering the appeal, the Arizona Court of Appeals examined whether the alleged obstruction of the view could support a private nuisance claim under state law. The court explained that such a claim requires more than a change in a neighbouring property’s use or appearance. Citing earlier Arizona decisions, it stated that the interference must be substantial, intentional and unreasonable under the circumstances and must cause significant harm. The court also noted that not every inconvenience or reduction in property value constitutes an actionable nuisance.The judgment addressed the legal position on scenic views directly. In paragraph 27, the court stated: “Arizona has never recognised a right to an unobstructed or scenic view across a neighbour’s property, and this court does not recognise such a right here.” It consequently concluded that the Pavlaks could not establish a nuisance claim based on the loss of a view caused by construction within the modified building envelope. The court also referred to decisions from other jurisdictions supporting the general rule that a lawful building does not become a private nuisance merely because it obstructs a neighbouring property’s view. It noted that a statute or easement could provide a different legal basis, but neither was at issue in this case.Arizona court dismisses claims over blocked views, privacy and rainwater runoffThe court also considered the Pavlaks’ concerns about privacy and potential rainwater runoff. On privacy, it found that Arizona had not recognised a private nuisance claim based on the kind of loss of privacy alleged in this case. The judges distinguished the dispute from cases involving more intrusive conduct, such as prolonged surveillance or the repeated direction of floodlights at a neighbour’s home. The court also noted that the Pavlaks had not alleged that Funk had modified the building envelope out of spite or malice.Regarding water runoff, the court acknowledged that interference with the flow of surface water could constitute a nuisance in appropriate circumstances. However, the Pavlaks had alleged only that the proposed house might alter rainwater flow and potentially cause water to enter their property. The construction had not yet taken place, and the alleged repeat water intrusion had not occurred. The court found these allegations insufficient to establish an actionable nuisance claim. It therefore affirmed the lower court’s judgment dismissing the claim and denied both parties’ requests for attorneys’ fees as sanctions on appeal. articles.title: Tell Modi to sack CEC, stir will stop in 30 sec: Rahul to traders
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Days after some traders raised concerns about the impact on business of ‘Chalo Delhi’ rally on Nov 1, Congress’s Rahul Gandhi urged the traders
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Days after some traders raised concerns about the impact on business of ‘Chalo Delhi’ rally on Nov 1, Congress’s Rahul Gandhi urged the traders to ask PM Narendra Modi to sack CEC Gyanesh Kumar to end the protests against ‘vote chori’.Rahul posted on X, “To every trader in Delhi: We love you and hear you. Government shut the metro, sealed the roads and locked down our capital. With a stolen vote, nothing is safe — your shop, savings, children’s future. Tell Modi to sack Gyanesh Kumar and the protests will stop in 30 seconds.”Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge also slammed govt for rising inflation during the festival season, and urged people to join the Ramlila Maidan rally.In what may add more friction to the already fraught govt-opposition ties, Centre has not given it’s go ahead for “mock Parliament” at Ashoka Hotel on Oct 30, whose centrepiece would be the symbolic impeachment of Kumar. Sources said the “mock Parliament” may now be held at Ramlila Maidan.Party’s K C Venugopal confirmed to TOI that permission has been refused. “Government is saying no to every venue we are requesting.”Get the latest India News and Live updates.
